title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is seeing a blend of new entrants challenging traditional satellite paradigms and established players enhancing their capabilities. Meanwhile, defense tech is inching closer to an IPO revival, with a notable focus on resilience and infrastructure.

themes.title: Challengers to Satellite Norms
themes.body: A startup is taking aim at the multi-orbit strategies that have long dominated satellite deployment. This could signal a shift in how companies approach orbital architecture and market competition.

themes.title: Defense Tech Funding Surge
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup has added $1.4 billion to space resilience efforts, highlighting a growing recognition of the need for robust space capabilities. This influx of cash could accelerate innovation and partnerships in the sector.

themes.title: New Collaborations in Space
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up for a tactical SDA constellation bid, indicating a trend toward collaboration among defense contractors. Such partnerships may streamline development and enhance operational capabilities.

themes.title: Hypersonic Hiccups Continue
themes.body: The latest hypersonic glide-vehicle test has slipped for the third consecutive quarter, raising questions about the pace of development in this critical area. This delay could have implications for national security and defense strategies.
